prompt:
An electric motor is represented by a quantitative Sankey diagram.
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Quantitative Sankey diagram for an electric motor. The input arrow enters horizontally on the left with a width of 60 mm, representing 1200 J of electrical energy. The arrow splits into two branches: a downward arrow of width 18 mm representing energy dissipated as heat in the windings and bearings, and a continuing horizontal arrow representing useful mechanical kinetic energy delivered to a conveyor belt.]
(a) Determine the scale of the Sankey diagram in joules per millimetre (J mm^-1). [1]
(b) Determine the useful mechanical energy delivered by the motor. [1]
(c) Calculate the efficiency of the motor. [1]
hints: In (a), divide the total input energy by the input arrow width.
In (b), subtract the wasted branch width from the input width, then multiply by the scale.
In (c), divide useful energy by total input energy.
solution:
(a) Scale = 1200 J / 60 mm = 20 J mm^-1.
(b) Useful arrow width = 60 mm - 18 mm = 42 mm. Useful mechanical energy = 42 mm * 20 J mm^-1 = 840 J. (Alternatively: wasted energy = 18 mm * 20 = 360 J; useful energy = 1200 J - 360 J = 840 J).
(c) Efficiency = (Useful energy output / Total energy input) = 840 J / 1200 J = 0.70 = 70%.
teacher_walkthrough: Step (a) checks ability to establish a scale factor from diagram dimensions.
Step (b) verifies conservation of arrow widths (Input = Useful + Wasted).
